 Order

This Writ Petition has been filed challenging the notification issued under Section 15(2) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001, dated 17.06.2013 and the consequential award passed by the second respondent, dated 26.02.2021 insofar as the property in S.No.83/2 measuring an extent of 153 sq.meters and S.No.83/3, measuring an extent of 309 Sq.meters and for a further direction to the second respondent to issue an amended notification.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.When the matter came up for hearing on 07.12.2023, this Court has passed the following order:
Heard the learned counsel on either side.
2.The short issue that arises for consideration in this case is that the service road that is proposed to be laid in TVS Nagar was to an extent of 7 meters on the Southern Side of the Bridge and 5.5 Meters on the Northern Side.

A representation was given by the residents of TVS Nagar to reduce the extent from 7 meters to 5.5 meters and they were also willing to permit their lands to be acquired if the service road is going to be laid only for 5.5 meters.

When a representation was made in this regard to the sixth respondent, the sixth respondent through letter dated 09.05.2016 communicated to the third respondent had taken into consideration the request made and also the decision that was taken insofar as this service road that was proposed to be laid at Madakulam and Jaihindpuram by reducing it from 7 meters to 5.5 meters and the sixth respondent has recommended for limiting the service road for TVS Nagar also to 5.5 meters.
This was also taken into consideration by this Court while admitting this Writ Petition and granting an interim order.

The sixth respondent has now filed Lakshmi Vidya Sangham vs The Secretary on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197488920/

sentences.text: the counter affidavit in this Writ Petition has not taken into consideration the earlier recommendation that was made through communication dated 09.05.2016.

The sixth respondent has stated in the counter affidavit that the service road is going to be laid only for 5.5 meters and that the balance of 1.50 meters is going to be utilized for providing a raised foot path and drain.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that insofar as the service road in Madakulam and Jaihindpuram, this foot path was laid within 5.5 meters that was utilized for the service road.

3.In the considered view of this Court, if the authorities have already taken a decision to confine the service road to 5.5 meters including the foot path in the other two areas at Madakulam and Jaihindpuram, the same should be applied in the case of TVS Nagar also.

4.The learned Additional Government Pleader seeks for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis some time to get instructions in this regard.
5.Post this case under the caption Part Heard Case on 14.12.2023.
3.When the matter came up for hearing today, the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents stated that the request made by the petitioner was considered by the Divisional Engineer and through a communication, dated 30.05.2017, made to the District Revenue Officer, Maduai, it was reiterated that an extent of 7 meters will have to be acquired, considering the fact that there is a school and the safety of the school children must be ensured.

The learned Additional Government Pleader further submitted that the decision that was taken insofar as the other two places, viz., Madakulam and Jaihind Puram, it will not apply insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned, since there is a school and the safety of the school children looms large.

4.Per contra, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the petitioner had volunteered to consent for the acquisition of 5.5 meters and accordingly, the petitioner had also re- arranged their property to enable the acquisition of 5.5 meters.

3 5.The learned Senior Counsel also brought to the notice of this Court the communication, dated 09.05.2016, made by the Divisional Engineer to the District Revenue Officer, Madurai.

6.By bringing to the notice of this Court the above two communications that were exchanged between the authorities, the learned Senior Counsel submitted that the genuine claim made by the petitioner was considered and it was decided to acquire 5.5 meters in order to provide for the service road.

However, there was a change in incumbent and he subsequently wrote a letter, dated 30.05.2017 informing the District Revenue Officer that the notification must be made for acquiring 7 meters insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned.

It was contended that the decision cannot keep changing whenever there is a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis change of incumbent and there must be some consistency followed to ensure the completion of laying of the service road.
The learned Senior Counsel submitted that the petitioner had consented for acquisition of 5.5 meters and there was no reason as to why the authorities were insisting for acquisition of 7 meters.
Accordingly, the learned Counsel sought for interference of the notification issued under Section 15(2) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act and the award proceedings initiated by the second respondent.
7.As recorded in the earlier order passed on 07.12.2023, there was a proposal to lay a service road.
It was proposed to be done in three places, viz., Madakulam, Jaihind Puram and TVS Nagar.
Insofar as Madakulam and Jaihind Puram, it was confined to 5.5 meters by reducing it from 7 meters, as was originally proposed.
However, insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned, the residents consented for the acquisition of 5.5 meters.

When a proposal was made to increase it to 7 meters, objections were given and it was properly considered and the District Revenue Officer in fact had recommended for modifying the extent in the notification in order to ensure speedy completion of the acquisition to lay https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis service road.
This was also followed up by the Divisional Engineer in letter dated 09.05.2016 giving reasons as to why the service road can be laid, even in TVS Nagar for 5.5 meters.
Within a year, the subsequent incumbent has taken a decision that insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned, 7 meters of lands must be acquired.

While taking this decision,
the Divisional Engineer does not even deal with the earlier decision that was taken on 09.05.2016 and assign any reason as to why he is differing with the decision that was taken by the earlier Divisional Engineer.
In view of inconsistent stand that has been taken by the authorities, the acquisition proceedings itself is stalled and there has been no progress for nearly ten years.

Lakshmi Vidya Sangham vs The Secretary on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197488920/
5 8.Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials that have been placed before this Court, this Court is of the firm view that the letter, dated 09.05.2016 issued by the sixth respondent can be taken note of and the acquisition can be confined to 5.5 meters even insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned.

If at all, there is some difficulty in future due to any reasons and if the authorities feel that more space is required for the service road insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned,
they can https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis go ahead and acquire additional lands by following due process of law.
This will ensure that the hands of the authorities are not tied down and it will always be left open to them to take appropriate action in future, if the need so arises.

9.In the light of the above discussion, there shall be a direction to the second respondent to issue a fresh notification under Section 15 of the Act by amending the earlier notification, dated 17.06.2013 and reduce the extent of lands to be acquired in TVS Nagar to 5.5 meters.
This process shall be completed by the second respondent within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Thereafter, the compensation shall be determined and paid to the land owners.
The said process shall be completed within a period of eight weeks thereafter.
In view of the same, it will be left open to the respondents to proceed further to lay the service road insofar as TVS Nagar is concerned.
10.This Writ Petition is disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
